title: fix(runtime): an in-process hook handler is handed the same ctx.title a hook body gets
body:
Part of #24289

Clause-②: no

Basis for the Clause-② line: `ctx.title(field?)`, which the served runtime already gives a hook `body`, is now also given to a hook's inline `handler` function on the in-process path. No request is newly accepted. No published TypeScript type gains a member: `HookContext` in `@objectstack/spec` is unchanged. No package entry exports anything new: `withInProcessHookTitle` is a module export of `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts`, and neither `sandbox/index.ts` nor the package `index.ts` re-exports it.

## What changed

- `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts`: `withInProcessHookTitle(handler, ql, hookName)` wraps a hook handler function. The function is called with a view of the engine's hook context that answers `title`, and the answer comes from `buildTitleSurface`, the same accessor the sandbox installs for a `body`. Its read channel and formula semantics (#24197, PR #24307) are not changed. The one edit to it is its return-type annotation (`NonNullable`), because it always returns the function. The view is a Proxy: every other read and every write goes to the engine's own context, so `ctx.input` and `ctx.result` writes land where the engine reads them, and the context object gains no key.
- `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`: `bindAppArtifactHandlers`, the one binder of an app's handlers, gives each hook whose `handler` is a function a copy with that function wrapped, before `ql.bindHooks`. The app's declaration is not rewritten. The engine's binder still decides whether `body` or `handler` runs.
- The handler sees what the VM delivers: the same one-argument call, and `null` (never the record's id) when there is no title. The read channel is the hook context's own `ctx.api`, read at call time, so a `runAs` hook reads under its declared identity. Two rules stay body-only: the reference form has no `api.read` gate (an in-process handler already holds `ctx.api`), and the stored-metadata family is not refused.

## Measured

- **Repro on main's runtime (A3).** `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` were restored to `ec749fbb4`, hash-equal to the base blobs. Runtime was rebuilt, and `withInProcessHookTitle` was absent from `packages/runtime/dist` (`scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs ... --absent`, exit 0). Then the new verify pin went red on the source door only, with `TypeError: ctx.title is not a function` (1 failed, 1 passed; the artifact door answered). The new runtime pin went red on both cases with the same TypeError. Both files were restored to HEAD (hash-equal, `git diff HEAD` empty) and runtime was rebuilt, with the marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. Both pins were then green. This was one run, recorded here and not kept as a test.
- **Why the wrap is in the runtime.** The suggested route was one new option for `bindHooksToEngine`, passed through the runtime's bind call. That option cannot be typed without editing two files outside this card's scope. The runtime calls `ql.bindHooks` through `IObjectQLEngine`, whose options type is in `packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`. `ObjectQL.bindHooks` declares its own options in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`. So the wrap happens in `packages/runtime` at bind time, and `packages/objectql` and `packages/spec` are not touched.
- **`os serve` over a config (A4).** This goes through the same code, so it is covered here. `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` mounts `new AppPlugin(config, ...)` when the config declares metadata and no AppPlugin is already present (line 3591 at `ec749fbb4`). `AppPlugin.start` binds through `bindAppArtifactHandlers` (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, line 1683). This was read from the code; no `os serve` process was started.
- **The published type (A5).** `HookContext` (`HookContextSchema`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`) declares no `title`, and this change does not add one. A `defineStack` inline handler's parameter is untyped (`HookSchema.handler` is a `(...args: any[]) => any` custom), so `ctx.title()` compiles there. A handler annotated `(ctx: HookContext)` gets TS2339 (measured with `tsc --strict` against the built spec at `a14895b71`). This is reported to the PM and not changed here.

## Tests

- `packages/verify/src/harness.hook-title-door.test.ts` (new) runs the same `beforeInsert` statements as an inline handler on a source boot and as a body on the artifact door, which is the shape `objectstack dev` serves. Both doors answer `{ own: 'L1 · Widget', product: 'Widget (W-1)', spare: 'null' }`. That is this record's one-hop formula title, the related record's own formula title, and `null` for an empty lookup.
- `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.hook-title.test.ts` (new) uses a real `ObjectQL` that dispatches through `triggerHooks`. It checks five things. Both forms answer, and an absent title is `null`. The related read goes once through the hook context's own `api`. Writes land on the engine's context. That context never gains a `title` key. The app's declaration keeps its own function.
- These local runs are at `a14895b71`, the final head, which is a merge of `origin/main` `51ad8e4fb`:
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 420 files passed; 6608 tests passed, 19 skipped.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify typecheck`: exit 0.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 42 files passed; 364 tests passed.
  - `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the four changed source and test files: exit 0, no findings.
  - The 63 families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, plus the 10 declared wide-population families whose population covers `packages/runtime` and `packages/verify`, all exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, no `dist/`). After a full `turbo run build`, it exited 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **The card's remaining slice: a `handler` that names a function.** #24289 remains open for it. This PR covers a hook whose `handler` is a function. A hook whose `handler` NAMES a function also runs in-process: that is the deprecated string form, and also what `objectstack build` ships for a callable it could not lower to a body. Such a hook is still not given `ctx.title`, because the engine's binder looks the function up by name after `bindAppArtifactHandlers` has run. Measured at `7bd31c8e5` in a one-off run that was not committed: `typeof ctx.title` was `'undefined'` in two cases. One was the artifact door with a `runtimeModule` and a string `handler`, which is the loader `os start --artifact` uses. The other was a source boot with `functions` and `handler: 'name'`. The same function as an inline handler answered. The measured route is one `bindHooksToEngine` option (`packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts`), plus the `IObjectQLEngine.bindHooks` options type (`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`, about line 396) and the `ObjectQL.bindHooks` options (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, about line 4849). That makes it a cross-lane slice, engine and spec.
- **`HookContext` declares no `title`.** `HookContextSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`) has no `title` member. Under `tsc --strict`, a handler annotated `(ctx: HookContext)` that calls `ctx.title()` gets TS2339, while an unannotated `defineStack` inline handler compiles. Declaring the member is a published-type change in the spec lane. It is sequenced after the slice above, so the declaration does not run ahead of what the runtime delivers.
- `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` is not edited. It already describes a `body` context as a subset of the in-process one, and this change makes that true for `ctx.title` on a function handler.
